name: Westinghouse automatic train braking
description: An automatic air brake system applied brakes in response to loss of train-line pressure.

places.note: Place refers to the sourced event; historic political boundaries are not inferred.

date.basis: Date stated in the cited source.

events.statement: A federal railway history dates Westinghouse’s introduction of the automatic air brake to 1872.

evidence.supports: ASME attributes automatic air-brake development and triple-valve refinement to George Westinghouse, contrasting it with the earlier direct-air brake. Its heading lists 1869 and 1872.
Federal report dates introduction of the automatic air brake to 1872.

events.caveats: The 1869 straight-air brake was a distinct earlier system; the source does not identify an exact 1872 deployment day.

contributions.resource: Developed the automatic train air brake

evidence.supports: ASME attributes automatic air-brake development and triple-valve refinement to George Westinghouse, contrasting it with the earlier direct-air brake. Its heading lists 1869 and 1872.

date.label: by 1880
date.basis: The library reports installations by 1880 without an exact first-use date.

events.statement: By 1880 automatic air brakes had been installed on locomotives and cars in the United States.

evidence.supports: Library says by 1880 Westinghouse automatic air brakes had been installed on 2,211 locomotives and 7,224 cars in the United States; it distinguishes his 1869 initial brake patent.

events.caveats: Counts are installed vehicles, not number of trains or a global adoption measure.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest event for this scoped capability established by the inspected passages; no global priority is inferred.

research.note: Source-backed admission; independent review pending. Independent reader checked FRA printed p. 8 on the 1872 introduction, ASME on development, and Linda Hall on the 1880 US installed vehicle counts.
